findings.possible_root_cause: Database has run out of connection slots
suggested_investigation: Close idle connections
Increase max_connections or use a pool
Check for connection leaks in the application
findings.example: FATAL remaining connection slots are reserved for non-replication superuser connections

findings.possible_root_cause: Node or volume has no free disk space
suggested_investigation: Check usage: df -h
Clean old images/logs (scripts/cleanup.sh)
Increase disk size or PVC size
findings.example: write error: No space left on device

suggested_investigation: Check database availability
Check network connectivity (service/DNS/ports)
Verify credentials in the Kubernetes Secret
Check connection limits and pool size
findings.example: ERROR database connection timeout after 30000ms host=db-service:5432

findings.possible_root_cause: Backend service is down, restarting or unreachable
suggested_investigation: Check pod status: kubectl get pods -n nexvion
Check service endpoints: kubectl get endpoints
Review readiness probe and recent rollouts
Check backend logs

findings.possible_root_cause: Container keeps crashing at startup or runtime
suggested_investigation: kubectl logs --previous <pod>
kubectl describe pod <pod>
Check config, environment variables and probes
Roll back: helm rollback nexvion
findings.example: Back-off restarting failed container web in pod nexvion-web-abc12

suggested_investigation: Check usage: kubectl top pods
Increase the memory limit in values.yaml
Look for memory leaks or traffic spikes

findings.possible_root_cause: Image tag missing in registry or AKS lacks pull permission
suggested_investigation: Verify the tag exists in ACR: az acr repository show-tags
Check AcrPull role: az aks update --attach-acr
Check image name and tag in values.yaml
findings.example: Warning Failed ErrImagePull: failed to pull image acrnexvionz034e.azurecr.io/nexvion-web:v99

findings.possible_root_cause: Service name does not resolve (wrong name or CoreDNS issue)
suggested_investigation: Verify the service name and namespace
Check CoreDNS pods in kube-system
Test: kubectl run -it --rm dns --image=busybox -- nslookup <name>
findings.example: dial tcp: lookup db-service: no such host

findings.possible_root_cause: Missing permission, bad credentials or probing of protected paths
suggested_investigation: Check source IP and request pattern for abuse
Verify RBAC and credentials
Consider rate limiting on the ingress

findings.possible_root_cause: Requests for missing files or routes (broken link or scanning)
suggested_investigation: Check for broken links in the frontend
Ignore if it is random bot traffic
